The first case they'll hear involves climate change. The city of Boulder, Colorado, is suing two big energy companies.
Boulder officials want the companies to share the cost of paying for disasters that are made worse by global warming.
The companies want to shift this argument from state courts, where it's been heard, to federal courts.
And Pierre's Kerry Johnson says the U.S. Supreme Court has other cases on its docket this term.
They do have some big cases already, including a challenge to state bans on the very popular AR-15 assault-style rifles.
There's going to be a clash over religion in schools, specifically a universal pre-K program in Colorado.
And there are a number of immigration cases brewing.
But the court is still adding new cases to the docket, so more is going to be coming.
And Pierre's Kerry Johnson reporting.
Cornell University is expected to announce this week which outside law firm will independently review its handling of rape allegations involving a former student.
And Pierre's Windsor-Johnson reports the case is prompting survivors of sexual assault to share and write about their own experiences.
Erin Smith of Winchester, Kentucky says reading about the Cornell allegations brought back feelings from an assault when she was 12 years old.
I was so enraged. I had to set my phone down and just pace around my kitchen like a caged tiger.
Trauma specialist Hannah Bronstein says for some survivors following the news coverage can feel like reliving an earlier assault.
Body flashbacks, not just memory flashbacks, they can almost transport them back there.
Bronstein says limiting time spent on news and social media or stepping away when it becomes overwhelming can help.
Windsor-Johnson, NPR News.
One American and two German scientists today have been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
NPR's Rob Stein reports it's for their fundamental discoveries that help explain how the brain works.
The Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute in Sweden awarded the prize to two German scientists, Peter Hegeman and Gerd Nagel,
and one American, Karl Deisserhof at Stanford University.
The three scientists played key roles in discoveries that led to light controlled switches that turned nerve cells on and off.
The technique opened a new way to understand the function of neurons known as optogenetics.
The Nobel Committee says the discoveries laid the foundation for a new era of neuroscience,
including helping to understand how the brain forms memories, feelings and behaviors.
Rob Stein, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The Pentagon says that it has brought home all its military bomber planes that were stationed at an air base in the United Kingdom.
This is the same air base where British authorities arrested five men last month.
They are suspected of plotting to attack the base.
The Defense Department says all the bombers have now been redeployed to their home stations in the United States.
In Brazil's presidential race, the right-wing opposition candidate is in the lead after almost all votes have been counted from yesterday's first round of voting.
It's an election with stakes that reach far beyond the South American country's borders.
Catherine Osborne has more from Rio de Janeiro.
In downtown Rio, supporters of left-wing president Luis Inacio Lula da Silva packed into this plaza, watching the results with anxiety.
Right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro outperformed polls and outperformed Lula to win the first round presidential vote.
He's promised to continue the legacy of his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.
In this election, right-wing politicians also grew in numbers in Brazil's Congress.
The presidential runoff is set for October 25th.
It's a contest President Trump is watching closely as he seeks greater U.S. influence in the region.
For NPR News, I'm Catherine Osborne in Rio de Janeiro.
Fire authorities in California say the bouquet fire north of Los Angeles is still growing.
It has scorched well over one mile of land, and it's nearly half-contained.
But fire authorities have put several areas under evacuation orders.
